CVE-2026-14620.467e840796033eac1e4c548817deec0bbea0e6a3: fix: constrain which file /open-editor opens, and who may ask Two gaps left by the fix for CVE-2026-14620, both reproduced against `main` before changing anything. **Which file.** The endpoint handed `fileName` straight to `launchEditor` with no check at all. The reference comes from the overlay, which sends webpack's module identifier out of a build error whose text a loader or a dependency writes — so it is not necessarily a file this project built. The advisory's own impact text names `~/.ssh/config`; only the caller half was addressed. The boundary is the compilation's own `fileDependencies` rather than containment against `compiler.context`. Module identifiers are absolute, and a monorepo sibling legitimately resolves outside the project root, so a context check would refuse files a developer has every reason to open: a file the build read 200 allowed a monorepo sibling the build read 200 allowed loader-prefixed reference 200 allowed a file in the project the build skipped 403 REFUSED outside the project entirely 403 REFUSED /etc/passwd 403 REFUSED **Who may ask.** `#isSameOriginRequest` treated "no `Origin`" as proof that no other origin's script sent the request. It is not: a browser omits Fetch Metadata for a destination that is not potentially trustworthy — plain `http` to anything but `localhost`, which `host: "0.0.0.0"` gives you — and a no-cors request such as `` carries no `Origin` either. A cross-site load therefore arrived with neither header and was indistinguishable from the overlay's own request: cross-site , plain-http LAN dest was 200, now 403 That is the same omission that defeated the earlier `Sec-Fetch` check in CVE-2026-6402, where the answer was a response header; here the request has a side effect on the developer's machine, so the request itself has to be refused. This costs `curl` access to both endpoints. Neither is documented, and the one test that asserted it ("e.g. curl") encoded the old reasoning rather than a contract, so it now asserts the refusal and says why.
